summary: Yonten Gonpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje. He later taught Dodrupchen Rinpoche and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Yoshiaki Shimizu specialized in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1968–1974) and held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1979) and Princeton University as Professor (~1984–2009).

Yoshifumi Honjo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1975). He held appointments at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University (~1999–2017), and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Yoshifumi Mizuno works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1978–1982) and the University of Tokyo (~1982–1985), later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (1986–1992) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1971) under Shoson Miyamoto and Shigeo Kamata, later serving as Lecturer (1971) and Professor (2001) at Komazawa University.

Yoshihiko Amino worked in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and held posts at Nagoya University (~1973–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1993).

Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and positions at Kongo Jushinkai and Kongo-ju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and later held positions there as a part-time lecturer and at the Kyogaku Dendo Research Center as a researcher (attested 2003).
Yoshihiro Hayashi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. In 2009, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University.

Yoshihito Muroji specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (1992) under Lambert Schmithausen, and held positions at Kyoto University, Koyasan University (attested 1995–2012), and Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2014–2015).
Yoshiki Motoaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshinobu Kimoto works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, and held positions at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College, Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and Ryukoku University (2013–2021).
Yoshinobu Sakade specialized in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1957) and under Mitsuji Fukunaga (~1957–1963), later holding a post at Kansai University (~1976–2005).

Yoshinori Takeuchi specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1933–1946) and held posts at Kyoto University (1948–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1978–1988).

Yoshinori Yasuda worked in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and Tohoku University (~1969–1975), and held posts at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, Tohoku University (~2012–2014), and Reitaku University (~2014).

Yoshio Kawakatsu worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1957–1960), and held a librarian-track assistant post at Kyoto University (~1952–1984).
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi was a Sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1907–1910) and held a post at Tohoku University (~1923–1946).

Yoshiro Imaeda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald and Rolf Alfred Stein, and served at the CNRS (~1974–2012) and Kyoto University (~2008–2012).
